notes.n4.hyper: The big US clouds plus Oracle hold most AI compute; China has its own top tier (Alibaba, Huawei, Tencent, Baidu, Volcano Engine).
notes.n4.neo: Neoclouds scaled on multi-billion contracts from Microsoft, Meta, OpenAI and Anthropic; CoreWeave and Nebius public, Nscale filed for IPO Sep-Oct 2026, Lambda preparing.
notes.n4.sovereign: Countries fund in-country compute via telcos and national champions (IndiaAI Mission, Humain, G42/Core42, EuroHPC AI Factories).
notes.n4.serverless: Per-second GPU platforms serve developers; consolidation under way (Cloudflare buying Replicate).
notes.n4.onprem: OEM 'AI factory' bundles co-engineered with NVIDIA dominate private AI.
notes.n4.market: Mix of centralised spot/forward markets (SF Compute, Vast.ai) and crypto-based DePIN networks.
notes.n4.finance: GPU-backed private credit from Magnetar, Blackstone, Blue Owl, Apollo and others funds neocloud build-outs; vendor backstops (e.g. NVIDIA capacity guarantees) are common.
notes.n4.orch: NVIDIA now owns the two most-used schedulers (Run:ai, Slurm); Kubernetes and Ray are the open alternatives.
notes.n4.finops: Generic FinOps vendors are adding GPU and AI-API cost views; few are GPU-native yet.
notes.n4.ops: GPU failure rates make health checks and fabric monitoring a differentiator; neocloud reliability is now rated independently (ClusterMAX).
notes.n4.offtake: computeprices.com tracks ~$1.05T across 21 disclosed lab-cloud deals (scale indicator, not audited)
notes.n4.confidential: Hyperscalers bundle GPU TEEs; independents being absorbed (Anthropic-OPAQUE, Oct 2026)
notes.n4.access: Mix of national research compute (NAIRR, AIRR, EuroHPC, IndiaAI) and vendor startup credits
